findings: The historical latency test ran src/test/gameLatency.test.ts under Vitest/jsdom, where Worker was undefined.
The historical stockfishService.initEngine() therefore returned false and analysis used the fallback path rather than a browser Stockfish worker.
The historical analyzer selected second-pass candidates only from facts whose source was real; consequently the historical run performed zero second-pass Stockfish searches.
The historical analyzer still stamped placeholder facts and the top-level result with stockfish_wasm, while the test printed and asserted that top-level label instead of observing worker searches.
The historical first pass did not forward the requested movetimeMs: 500 value into analyzeFen.
conclusion: The 5365 ms number is a fallback/hardcoded-source result and is not a valid real-WASM comparator. The fresh browser benchmark is the first truthful baseline: median 42728 ms, max 42934 ms, with 83/83 observed real worker searches per run and all runs below the historical 60000 ms per-run gate. No product timing was weakened to manufacture a comparison.
